title: PopQA question record (uncertainty study)
description: One question of the PopQA set (long-tail facts) used by thesis Objectives 1-2. Mirrors the Item dataclass in uncertainty/sets/load.py.
x-format: JSON Lines: one JSON object per line, each matching this schema
x-source: akariasai/PopQA (test.tsv); evidence: English Wikipedia page summaries
x-note: Documentation only: no code reads this schema.

id.description: Unique question id in this set: 'popqa-' + the source dataset's own id.

set.description: Name of the question set: always 'popqa'.

kind.description: Answer kind 'short': free-text answer, graded by an LLM judge from another model family.

question.description: The question as sent to the model.

answers.description: Accepted answers: the dataset's possible_answers (the object's name and its aliases).

split.description: Fixed, seeded split: dev (30%) only tunes thresholds and trains the Objective 2 models; every reported number uses test (70%).

core.description: true if the question is in the core tier, the subset every model answers; the file itself is the extended tier.

judge_mode.description: How the LLM judge grades a free-text answer: match (agrees with a reference answer), truthfulqa (TruthfulQA judge prompt), abstain (correct only if it says the question cannot be answered), premise (correct only if it rejects the false premise). Unused for rule-graded kinds.

incorrect_answers.description: Known false answers from the dataset (TruthfulQA only; empty elsewhere).

gold_type.description: Always null: the dataset gives no uncertainty type for these questions.

evidence.description: Introduction of the subject's English Wikipedia article (at most 800 characters); it may not state the answer. Used only by the Objective 2 knowledge intervention.

hint.description: Always null: this set has no hint.

s_pop.description: Popularity of the subject: monthly Wikipedia page views, from PopQA.

pop_bin.description: Popularity bin: quintile of log10(s_pop), 0 = rarest, 4 = most popular. Used to stratify the sample.

prop.description: The Wikidata relation the question asks about.

subject.description: The subject entity of the question.

wiki_title.description: English Wikipedia title of the subject (used to fetch the evidence).

meta.description: Extra fields kept from the source dataset (for strata and analysis).

examples.question: What is Mamuju the capital of?
examples.evidence: Mamuju is the capital of the Indonesian province of West Sulawesi. The town was formerly part of South Sulawesi province.
